fields.name: Arizona Mist System
fields.room: Tech Shed / Bridge / Furnace Room / Bog / Graveyard
fields.outputs: Property-wide mist; Bridge branch; Furnace Room branch with two steam-simulation valves; Bog branch; Graveyard branch
fields.controller: Arizona Mist machine local controls — exact model TBD
fields.maintenanceLog: HollowNet maintenance record required: log date, operator, pump/filter/nozzle/valve inspection or service, leaks, repairs, winterization, recommissioning and notes. No service events are recorded yet.
fields.notes: Confirmed walkthrough: one large Arizona Mist machine in the Tech Shed serves the property. Distribution lines branch to the Bridge, Furnace Room, Bog and Graveyard. The Furnace Room branch has two valves that simulate steam escaping through pipes. The machine starts from a manual switch and remains completely local; the Main Hub provides documentation only, including reference material, maintenance history and notes. Attach the exact model, manual, plumbing map, valve labels and service instructions when available.

fields.power: Three to four 120 V AC projectors; media-player supply — TBD
fields.outputs: Three to four silent window projections; no audio
fields.trigger: Local power; automatic media-loop startup desired
fields.notes: Confirmed walkthrough: Facade Windows is a separate planned projection scene from Mia & Roy. It will use approximately three to four projectors, remain completely local and have no audio. The desired behavior is for the media player and projection loop to start automatically when powered. Final projector count/models, player architecture, synchronization and automatic projector startup method remain TBD.

Confirmed walkthrough: the Front Porch Rocking Chair uses a 12 V DC wiper motor and a local timer relay to repeat its rocking loop. It remains completely local with no HollowNet operational control. Exact rocking/rest intervals and the upstream power-switch behavior remain to be documented.

fields.power: Separate supplies: 5 V DC ESP32 and dedicated high-current servo supply — servo voltage/current TBD
fields.outputs: Version-one head and hand/arm movement; possible future weight shift
fields.trigger: Randomized movement approximately every 45 seconds by default, Hub-adjustable; either actor button or motion sensor — selection TBD; Hub test/control
fields.network: Wi-Fi to Front House Zone Controller
fields.notes: Confirmed walkthrough: version one of the planned Suit of Armor uses an ESP32 HollowNet node with both head and hand/arm movement. A weight-shift effect remains a possible future addition. Normal behavior selects a randomized movement approximately every 45 seconds by default; the cadence is adjustable from the Hub. One external trigger type may be added—either an actor button or a motion sensor, not both—with the selection still TBD. The ESP32 and servos use separate power supplies. The Hub must show online/status/fault information and provide enable, disable, individual movement tests and scene-control commands. Servo count, motion limits and servo-supply voltage/current remain TBD. Any weight-shift mechanism requires a secured base, mechanical stops and stability testing before operation.

fields.outputs: Front House commands, status aggregation and service controls; Suit of Armor enable/test/control
fields.notes: Front House zone boundary for Facade Windows, Front Porch and Reception Room. The Suit of Armor is the first planned connected field node and reports online/status/fault data while accepting Hub enable, disable, movement-test and scene-control commands. Facade Windows and the Rocking Chair remain local.

fields.power: 5 V DC Raspberry Pi 4; connected scene hardware supplies — TBD
fields.outputs: 45-second coordinated lighting, audio and bass-shaker scene
fields.trigger: Program auto-starts with Pi power; doorbell button starts scene when ready; button is ignored during 45-second run
fields.controller: Raspberry Pi 4; also serves as First Room Controller
fields.network: Wi-Fi to Upper House Zone Controller
fields.notes: Confirmed walkthrough: Mrs. Grimm is both the First Room scene and its room controller; no separate CTL-011 hardware is required. The scene program starts automatically whenever the Pi receives power. A doorbell button pressed as the group enters starts the complete coordinated lighting, audio and bass-shaker scene when ready. Additional button presses are ignored during the 45-second sequence; afterward it automatically resets and returns to ready. The Hub provides the only status indicator—Pi online plus ready, running and fault state—and provides scene test and reset controls. No physical room status light is required.

fields.power: Two separately switched branches: one switch for both projector/media-player systems; one switch for the 120 V AC continuous-duty crank motor — exact ratings TBD
fields.outputs: Two autoplay projection loops; crank-driven raising and lowering of six articulated spiders
fields.trigger: Two manual power switches operate independently: projector switch starts both autoplay loops; motor switch starts continuous crank motion
fields.controller: Local autoplay media players and direct-powered crank mechanism
fields.maintenanceLog: HollowNet maintenance record required: log date, operator, both projectors/media players, 120 V motor, crank arm, six articulated spiders, monofilament lines, attachment points, repairs and notes. No service events are recorded yet.
fields.notes: Confirmed walkthrough: the Sitting Room Spiders effect uses two projectors that automatically play continuous loops. Both projector/media-player systems are controlled by one manual power switch. A separate manual power switch controls the continuously running 120 V motor, which drives a crank arm that raises and lowers six articulated spiders on monofilament. The crank geometry causes the spiders to rise and fall at different times and speeds. The entire effect remains local with no Hub operational control. Projector/media-player models and the motor rating remain to be documented.

fields.power: 5 V DC Raspberry Pi; scene lighting and actor/drop equipment supplies — details TBD

fields.trigger: Hanging actor uses local remote to start 20-second scene; manual actor reset required after every run
fields.maintenanceLog: HollowNet maintenance record required: log date, operator, trigger remote, Raspberry Pi, skeleton-reflection lighting, actor reveal lighting, hanging/drop equipment, physical safety inspection, manual reset check, repairs and notes. No service events are recorded yet.
fields.notes: Confirmed walkthrough: the Library Hanging Transformation is a 20-second local actor scene. The hanging actor starts the sequence with a remote. Lighting flashes on a reflected skeleton positioned over the real actor, then changes from the skeleton image to the live actor as the actor drops down. After each performance, the actor must manually reset the effect before it can run again. The Raspberry Pi and scene remain completely local with no Hub operational control. Exact lighting channels, remote type, power distribution, actor/drop equipment and reset procedure remain to be documented.
